basics.name: Plastics makers' snap-fit design guides: Covestro (formerly Bayer) 'Snap-Fit Joints for Plastics - A Design Guide'; BASF 'Snap-Fit Design Manual' (Technical Expertise series); DuPont 'General Design Principles for DuPont Engineering Polymers - Design Guide Module I' (chapter 10 on snap-fits and press fits)
basics.url: Covestro guide (26 pages, official PDF): https://solutions.covestro.com/-/media/covestro/solution-center/brands/downloads/imported/1557218421.pdf (identical copies at https://solutions.covestro.com/-/media/covestro/solution-center/brands/downloads/imported/1557216102.pdf and https://www.covestro.com/-/media/covestro/solution-center/brands/downloads/imported/1556891135.pdf?rev=a81fb62f7f9948afb36e7602d237e912) ; Covestro companion 'Engineering Polymers Joining Techniques Design Guide': https://solutions.covestro.com/-/media/covestro/solution-center/brands/downloads/imported/1556890495.pdf?rev=6035fb2043ef4fd8b536fdb54abf6939 ; BASF manual: no BASF-hosted copy found; full copy filed as a public exhibit at the US Patent Trial and Appeal Board: https://ptacts.uspto.gov/ptacts/public-informations/petitions/1529702/download-documents?artifactId=qS3ulmCY5CWcGMJ3BonZ4Z1aucAGL4RFnzzCy4zxr4ZvIGobt8dq-u4 ; BASF online Snapfit Calculator (registration): https://plastics-rubber.basf.com/northamerica/en/performance_polymers/services/service_calculation_programmes ; DuPont Module I (136-page PDF hosted by distributor Distrupol): https://www.distrupol.com/General_Design_Principles_for_Engineering_Polymers.pdf

basics.authority_level: manufacturer (material suppliers' application engineering departments); the BASF short-beam correction cites its own SPE ANTEC 1987 paper and was checked by FEA and part tests; these guides are the standard references cited by Wikipedia, textbooks and 3D-printing snap-fit studies

coverage.covers: Snap-fit joints (clip joints) in thermoplastics. Covestro: general principles, types (cantilever, U-shaped, torsion, annular), cantilever design with 4 beam-shape designs and 4 cross-sections, permissible undercut, deflection and mating forces, torsion snap joints, annular snap joints, the case where both mating parts flex, and worked examples (e.g. a traffic light held together only by snaps, incl. a bayonet-style sun visor and a push-to-release hook). BASF: why use snaps, types (cantilever, U- and L-shaped cantilevers, cylindrical/annular mentioned), classical beam theory, an improved method for short beams using a 'deflection magnification factor' Q, formulas for L- and U-shaped snaps, and failure causes (stress concentration, creep/stress relaxation, fatigue). DuPont Module I: cylindrical (annular) undercut snap-fits and cantilever lug snap-fits inside a wider guide that also covers press fits, self-tapping screws, springs, plastic bearings, plastic gears (spur, helical, worm, bevel), combined-function gears (ratchet plus gear, torque-limiting gear, slip coupling, backlash-free flexible gear), spin, ultrasonic, vibration and hot-plate welding, riveting and design for disassembly. About 4 to 6 snap-fit types in total
coverage.organisation: By snap-fit type (by how the hook bends: bending, twisting, hoop stretching), then by calculation step (allowed strain, deflection, force to push together, force to pull apart), with worked examples. DuPont is organised by design topic and assembly technique. Clear once you know the words 'undercut', 'strain' and 'secant modulus'; a beginner can follow the pictures and the worked examples but not the equations without help
coverage.scope_match: high for the snap-fit family, which is a top priority for 3D printing (cantilever, U/L-shaped, torsion and annular snaps, separable vs permanent, push-to-release), and DuPont adds in-scope plastic mechanisms (ratchet gears, torque-limiting gears, slip couplings, integral springs); low for breadth, as they cover only plastics joining and are written for injection moulding
coverage.taxonomy_used: By loading mode of the flexing feature (Covestro's 4 basic shapes): cantilever snap joints (bending), U-shaped snap joints (a cantilever variant), torsion snap joints (shear in a torsion bar), annular snap joints (rotationally symmetric, multiaxial hoop strain). BASF: cantilever, 'U' shaped cantilever, 'L' shaped cantilever, plus cylindrical. DuPont: 2 categories, cylindrical undercut snap-fits and cantilever lug snap-fits. All also split joints by the return angle into separable (removable) and inseparable (permanent)
coverage.example_types: cantilever snap-fit hook (tapered-thickness and tapered-width versions); U-shaped snap arm; L-shaped snap (slot in base wall); torsion snap joint / snap-fitting rocker arm on a torsion bar (press one end to release); continuous annular snap joint (lamp cover, semi-hermetic); discontinuous (slotted) annular snap joint; cylindrical snap-fit of a steel shaft into a plastic hub; positive-locking segmented undercut with 90-degree return; push-to-release snap (press tongues to free the arms); rigid lug plus snap hook on the opposite side; bayonet-style sun-visor catch; snap-fit ball bearing retention; snap-together split worm gear; molded-in spring on a ratchet wheel (DuPont); torque-limiting gear with pivoting springs (DuPont); gear with sliding (slip) coupling on a split hub (DuPont); backlash-free flexible (ovalised) gear that slips at end stops (DuPont); press fit / interference fit
coverage.making_methods: Injection-moulded thermoplastics (PC, PC/ABS, PBT, nylon, acetal, PET, PEI, ABS and glass-filled grades); mould-tooling notes (slides, slots to avoid side cores). The equations transfer to 3D-printed and machined plastic parts but the guides say nothing about printing
coverage.item_count: Covestro snap-fit guide: 26 pages, sections A to F, 29 figures, 3 tables, 3 worked examples. BASF: 24 pages, 6 parts, about 5 worked examples. DuPont Module I: 136 pages (snap-fits about 4 pages, pp. 72-76, plus about 2 pages of combined-function gear examples, 6 figures)
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: hand-release only / separable vs permanent: yes (return angle sets whether the joint can be pulled apart; push-to-release tongues; 90-degree return for permanent joints; torsion rocker arm opened by pressing). Compliant: yes, snap-fits are flexure joints, and DuPont covers integral plastic springs. Torque-limiting: yes in DuPont (torque-limiting gear with pivoting springs; slip coupling on a split hub; flexing gear that slips at a stop). One-way/ratchet: yes in DuPont (ratchet wheel with molded-in springs). Gear trains: DuPont Module I has full plastic gear design chapters (spur, helical, worm, bevel). Indexing/detent: only through the 'pressure point' lugs holding a door open in Covestro [uncertain]. Self-locking and over-centre: no. Print-in-place: no. Powered connectors: no. Adhesives: not in the snap-fit guides; Covestro's companion joining guide covers solvent bonding and adhesive types for PC (two-part epoxy and urethane give strong bonds; cyanoacrylate is fast but can attack stressed polycarbonate and is brittle), and DuPont compares bonding with other assembly techniques
coverage.entry_structure: Per snap-fit type: description with application photos, a sketch with symbols, calculation equations (deflection, strain, deflection force, mating and separation force), material data tables (allowable strain, friction coefficient, secant modulus curves), worked numerical examples and design hints
coverage.audience_level: professional (plastic part designers and engineers); usable by undergraduates and advanced hobbyists

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: medium: short plain-English introductions and many real-product photos (fuse box, wheel cover, lamp housing, traffic light), but the core is equations with engineering symbols (strain, secant modulus, section modulus), and imperial/metric mixed units
usefulness.has_images: yes: line drawings of each snap type, application photos, graphs (stress concentration vs fillet radius, secant modulus, magnification factor Q); good quality in the Covestro and BASF PDFs, scanned-looking in the DuPont PDF [uncertain]
usefulness.gaps: No guidance for 3D printing (layer direction, lower printed strain limits, PLA/PETG values, clearances); materials limited to each maker's own resins; no snap-fit families such as ball-and-socket clips, living-hinge latches or print-in-place clips; torsion and annular sections are short; no interactive calculator except BASF's behind login; equations need unit care; no selector comparing snap-fit with other joints except DuPont's short table
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: fair: each guide is a stable-looking single PDF (e.g. https://solutions.covestro.com/-/media/covestro/solution-center/brands/downloads/imported/1557218421.pdf) that can be linked from snap-fit entries with a page number; no per-type web pages; company media URLs have changed before (Bayer to Covestro) and BASF's own copy has vanished, so add a note of title and edition
usefulness.reusable_data: not reusable as data (all rights reserved PDFs); the equations, allowable-strain values and friction coefficients are facts that can be restated in our own words with a citation
usefulness.maintained: Static documents: Covestro PDF is the 10/2015 edition, still online in 2026; BASF manual (2007) is no longer found on BASF's site, but BASF offers an online Snapfit Calculator; DuPont Module I (2000) survives on distributor sites, not on an official DuPont or Celanese page that we opened
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) Classify snap-fits by what flexes: bending hook (cantilever), longer bending path (U or L shape), twisting bar (torsion), stretching ring (annular); a clear first split for the snap-fit family. (2) Explain 'removable or permanent' by the back angle of the hook (return angle), which maps directly onto our removability filter. (3) Show one fully worked example per type, in plain numbers. (4) A 'both parts flex' note and 'use 60% of the strain for joints opened often' rule are good one-line tips. (5) A small comparison table of assembly methods (screw, snap-fit, press-fit, welding, bonding, overmolding) against material mix, recyclability and disassembly (DuPont Table 11.01) is a model for our flow-chart comparison pages. (6) Real product photos (battery lid, fuse box, wheel cover) help beginners recognise each type
usefulness.design_rules_given: Yes, many numbers: Covestro allowable short-term strain at 23 C (Makrolon PC 4%, Bayblend PC/ABS 2.5%, Makroblend 3.5%, Apec 4%, 10% glass PC 2.2%, 20% glass PC 2.0%); use about 60% of these for frequent separation; partly crystalline plastics up to near yield, amorphous up to about 70% of yield strain, glass-filled about half the elongation at break; tapering thickness to half at the tip allows over 60% more deflection; root radius not less than 0.015 in (about 0.4 mm), R/h about 0.6 limit; friction coefficients for 13 plastics on steel; mating force W = P(mu + tan a)/(1 - mu tan a); annular joint remote from the tube end needs about 3 times the force. BASF: fillet radius at least 0.5 t; beam formulas valid above L/t about 10, correction factor Q below that; allowable strains (e.g. PC 4-9.2%, acetal 7%, nylon 6 8% dry, PBT 8.8%, ABS 6-7%, 30% glass grades about 2%); friction coefficients for 8 plastics; 90-degree return angle to resist relaxation. DuPont: allowable strains for lug snap-fits used once vs frequently (e.g. Delrin 100: 8% / 2-4%; Zytel 101 dry 4% / 2%; glass-filled Zytel 0.8-1.2% / 0.5-0.7%; Hytrel 20% / 10%); cylindrical snap-fit undercut table for shaft diameters 2-35 mm; 45-degree return angle for removable, 90 degrees for permanent, 30-degree lead-in
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: No generator in the PDFs; BASF offers an online Snapfit Calculator (registration required, not tested)
usefulness.terminology_value: high for snap-fit terms and their aliases: snap joint / snap-fit, cantilever snap (hook, lug, finger), U-shaped and L-shaped snaps, torsion snap joint (rocker arm), annular or cylindrical snap joint (bead and groove), undercut, overhang, lead (entrance) angle, return (retraction) angle, mating force, separation / pull-off force, permissible strain, secant modulus, deflection magnification factor
usefulness.decision_support: Limited: rules of thumb for choosing a type (U or L shapes when a straight cantilever would be over-strained; annular when high-elongation unfilled plastic is used; cantilever lugs for non-round parts); separable vs inseparable guidance by return angle; DuPont's comparison table of assembly techniques (screw, snap-fit, press-fit, welding, bonding, overmolding) by material combination, recyclability and disassembly. No flow chart
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Covestro guide is the Bayer guide rebranded (Bayer Corporation 1996 edition per search snippet [uncertain]); BASF builds on classical beam theory and its own 1987 SPE ANTEC short-beam paper (Lee, Dubin and Jones) and cites Trantina (1989) and Trumbull (1984) for strain values. All three overlap heavily with each other, with Bonenberger's 'The First Snap-Fit Handbook' (not opened) [uncertain], with Wikipedia's Snap-fit article (cantilever, torsional, annular) and with 3D-printing service guides (Protolabs, Formlabs, Xometry) that restate these equations (not checked here) [uncertain]. Companion guides: Covestro 'Engineering Polymers Joining Techniques Design Guide' (screws, inserts, ultrasonic, welding, solvent and adhesive bonding) and later DuPont modules on specific resins
